It presents the same cluster of achievements later attributed to McCloy: an effective nuclear-test-ban treaty, a comprehensive program for general and complete disarmament, negotiations with the Soviet Union, and creation of a disarmament agency. C10 is exceptionally strong for the narrower passage about McCloy's organizational study, recommendations, and proposed agency, while C21 offers only a more general commendation structure.","shared_material":[{"child_excerpt":"the Government has been able to table at Geneva a workable, effective and understandable draft treaty for the banning of nuclear weapons tests","parent_excerpt":"The United States continues to believe that conclusion of an adequately controlled test ban agreement is a matter of greatest urgency... our continued willingness to negotiate an effective treaty","explanation":"Both describe the American effort to obtain an effective, controlled nuclear-test-ban treaty through negotiations."},{"child_excerpt":"your development of the United States Program for General and Complete Disarmament in a Peaceful World has set forth clearly the proposals of the United States","parent_excerpt":"The study has also resulted in the development of a comprehensive plan for general and complete disarmament which is in the final stage of preparation for public presentation.","explanation":"This is the same distinctive disarmament program, described in closely parallel terms as a newly developed comprehensive United States plan."},{"child_excerpt":"You have also performed a valuable service in connection with the establishment of a permanent agency of the Government to deal with the problems of disarmament and arms control.","parent_excerpt":"For some months the United States has been conducting an intensive study of the problem of general disarmament which resulted in a request to Congress to create a disarmament agency.","explanation":"Both connect the disarmament study directly to the congressional effort to establish a permanent specialized agency."},{"child_excerpt":"the intransigence of others, especially on the issue of control over nuclear testing, has brought disappointment to the world","parent_excerpt":"The Soviet resumption of atmospheric testing... The United States is pleased to note... the importance of an effective system of inspection and control. This is the crux of the matter.","explanation":"The child's concluding contrast condenses C07's account of Soviet obstruction and the central dispute over inspection and control."}]}
